scope_note: SINGLE-APPLICATION SCOPE. This schema models a portfolio-wide identity landscape, but this dispatch covered exactly one application (d634afdb-97cc-4589-a080-5766d4f377d5, 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata'). Nothing here characterises the wider faa portfolio: no other application's source was read, so the absence of Login.gov, PIV/MyAccess, AD/IWA or SAML below is a statement about THIS application only, not a portfolio finding. A genuine proliferation analysis needs a multi-application dispatch.
methodology_note: Derived from negative evidence over all 22 git-tracked files. Greps for identity|principal|authenticat|authoriz|oauth|saml|ldap|login.gov|piv|password|credential|token across *.cs, *.config, *.csproj, *.ps1, *.bat and *.sln returned only three false positives — the PublicKeyToken attributes on the xUnit assembly references at src/GildedRose.Tests/GildedRose.Tests.csproj:46, :50 and :54. There is no authentication code, no authorization check, no session, no user record, no credential store and no directory or IdP integration of any kind.

user_classes: local-interactive-operator (whoever holds an interactive Windows session on the host; identified and authorised solely by the OS login, which this application never reads)
evidence_citations: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:8 — `static void Main(string[] args)` is the only entry point; no authentication, authorization or principal lookup precedes the business logic at Program.cs:31

src/GildedRose.Console/app.config:1-6 — the entire configuration file is <startup><supportedRuntime>; no <authentication>, <membership>, <roleManager>, <identity>, <authorization> or <connectionStrings> element exists

src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:33 — System.Console.ReadKey() confirms an interactive local operator is the only actor; there is no network listener, so there is no remote authentication surface to assess
negative grep (whole tree): zero occurrences of WindowsIdentity, IPrincipal, ClaimsPrincipal, FormsAuthentication, OAuth, SAML, OpenIdConnect, LDAP, DirectoryEntry, Login.gov or PIV

assurance_gaps.description: The application performs no identity proofing because it establishes no identity at all: it is a local console executable with a single Main() entry point (src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:8) and no user concept. Severity is LOW rather than high because the exposure is bounded by the host OS session — there is no listener, no persisted data and no PII (the only values handled are fictional retail item names and two integers, Program.cs:16-26) — so there is nothing an unproofed actor can reach beyond a local process that prints one greeting and exits.
assurance_gaps.remediation_recommendation: Nothing to remediate in place. This becomes a real gap only if the target design exposes this logic as a service or API — at that point the new surface must inherit the portfolio's federated identity decision (see broker_recommendation) rather than invent a per-app model. Record it as a target-state obligation on the Design line, not as a legacy defect.

assurance_gaps.description: No MFA, because there is no first authentication factor to add a second to: no credential is collected, validated or stored anywhere in the tree (app.config carries only a <supportedRuntime> element, and no *.cs file references any credential or authentication type). Reported explicitly so a reviewer can distinguish 'MFA absent because authentication is absent by design' from 'MFA missing from an authenticated application', which is a materially different risk.
assurance_gaps.remediation_recommendation: Not applicable to the as-is application. If the migration target is interactive or API-reachable, require phishing-resistant AAL2+ (PIV or FIDO2) on the new surface and do not carry forward any email- or SMS-code pattern.

proliferation_findings_note: Deliberately empty and NOT a skipped check. Every finding_type in this schema's vocabulary asserts a relationship between two or more identity models, applications or accounts; this dispatch observed one application carrying zero identity models, so none of them can be evidenced. Emitting 'identity-model-per-app' here would be a fabricated portfolio claim from a single-app sample. Re-run across the full application roster to populate this array.

broker_recommendation.broker_technology: none required for the as-is application
broker_recommendation.rationale: There is no identity surface to front: no listener, no session, no user store, no credential. Bringing this application behind a federated broker would mean inventing an authentication requirement the legacy system never had. 'keep-separate' is the honest as-is answer — it records that this application contributes nothing to a broker design and should not be counted as an in-scope relying party. If the Design line exposes the nightly inventory update as a service, the broker decision must be made against that NEW surface and against the wider portfolio, using a multi-application identity-landscape run rather than this single-app record.
